sophia: Heads-up — saw a p99 jump on hosted API around 12:02 UTC. p95 moved 180ms->420ms, p99 to ~2.1s. Queue depth on pool-A spiked to 96 for a few minutes. Anyone seen this? :eyes:
perf-bot: Alert: p99 latency > 2s for /v1/generate (6m). Affected hosts: pool-A-1,pool-A-2,pool-A-3. No user-facing deploys in last 30m.
marcus: digging into traces — most time is waiting in the queue layer. Kernel selection logs show repeated fallback to generic kernel when batch_size == 1. Snippet:
```
kernel_select: {model: redwood-13b, requested_seq: 512, batch_size: 1, chosen: generic_kernel, reason: "no optimized kernel for bs=1"}
```
ada: KV cache telemetry shows a huge hit-rate drop at the same window. Before: hit_rate=0.89; during spike: hit_rate=0.07. Sample metric: `kv_cache.hits=12 kv_cache.misses=158 kv_cache.latency_ms=1.2` — looks like hot-key eviction/thrashing.
kevin: infra graphs show CPU steal and IO compaction on the VMs that host pool-A-2 around 12:00 — possible noisy neighbor. vm-analytics-3 had a compaction job at 11:58 that correlates. :thinking_face:
mike: batching telemetry: distribution shifted hard to the left — median batch size went from 6 -> 1. Continuous-batching timeout fired a lot. I suspect yesterday's change to avoid cross-tenant batching (queue-merging=false) caused many small batches to be flushed immediately. @ada did you flip that flag?
ada: yeah I toggled queue-merging=false for a pilot (SLO-sensitive tenants) yesterday afternoon. I thought it only affected a small set, but looks like routing overlapped with a busy tenant and propagated more widely. Reverting in staging now. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1234 :construction:
marcus: GPU profiling confirms higher per-token overhead when generic kernel chosen. Optimized path: `kernel_launch_ms ≈ 0.9` generic path: `kernel_launch_ms ≈ 3.1` — ~3x overhead which explains p99 moving into seconds for single-token-heavy requests.
sophia: Proposed mitigations: 1) revert the queue-merge flag (ada) 2) temporarily increase per-tenant queue cap from 32 -> 64 to reduce immediate flushes 3) route affected tenant traffic to dedicated low-latency pool while we observe. Also add a short-term KV cache warmup for hot keys. Thoughts? :thumbsup:
ada: on it — reverting queue-merging in canary now. Also adding a small jitter to batching timers to avoid synchronized flushes.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for infra change (PR #1234) on pool-A-1.
marcus: also opened a profiling ticket to get more granular breakdown of kernel selection reasons (RED-4579). We should track batch_size distribution as a first-class metric.
sophia: thanks everyone. If canary looks good, promote and watch p95/p99 for 30m. Filed follow-up for KV cache instrumentation and automatic warmup: RED-4580. :eyes: :fire:
